title: 3am cron ran sync-to-r2 even after a failed pull/build; after the 6/30 schema bump it could publish a new-schema R2 manifest over stale parquets
tier_reason: latent, no evidenced firing: the harmful combination (new SCHEMA_VERSION + ungated sync) never ran a 3am chain, because the gated line was installed and exercised by the 7/01 3am run; before the bump an ungated sync after a failed build re-uploaded the prior consistent data. Kept for restore coverage (R2 is a restore source)

contract.text: The 3am chain publishes an R2 manifest only after a successful pull and build, so the manifest's schema_version always describes the parquets actually uploaded.
contract.source: scripts/cron-setup-hetzner.sh 3am-chain comment (b0420a0); src/bts/data/schema.py SCHEMA_VERSION comment (loaders compare it with the R2 manifest.json and refuse a mismatch)

mechanism.text: the installed 3am line was `(pull && build && preview ; sync-to-r2)`, so sync-to-r2 ran whenever the chain reached it, including after a failed pull or build; once 793a093 added the is_resumed_portion column (changing SCHEMA_VERSION, the hash of PA_COLUMNS), a failed 2026 rebuild would have uploaded a manifest stamped with the new schema_version over the stale old-schema parquets

residual.text: A crash or R2 outage part-way through sync could still leave the manifest and uploaded objects inconsistent until content-addressed keys made the manifest flip the only commit point (7/10).

watchdog.trigger: after each 3am chain, cron.log shows sync-to-r2 running in a chain whose pull or build exited nonzero, or the R2 manifest's schema_version differs from the SCHEMA_VERSION of the parquets uploaded in that run
watchdog.recovery_assertion: a restore read of the R2 manifest and parquets loads with matching schema_version and row counts equal to the local 2026 build

evidence.locator: commit b0420a0 message body and diff (scripts/cron-setup-hetzner.sh)
evidence.what: the `;` before sync-to-r2 let it run after a failed pull/build; with the is_resumed_portion SCHEMA_VERSION bump a failed rebuild could publish a new-schema manifest over stale parquets; surfaced by the post-deploy Codex review (no firing reported)
introduced the `preview ; sync-to-r2` ordering so preview survives an R2 outage; the ungated sync dates from here

evidence.locator: commit 793a093 diff (src/bts/data/schema.py PA_COLUMNS); schema.py SCHEMA_VERSION definition at 63fd1d0
evidence.what: SCHEMA_VERSION is a hash of PA_COLUMNS, so adding is_resumed_portion (2026-06-30 13:54 ET) changed it
verified live on the box: 'full set installed + firing; 3am pipeline ran clean today (pull → build → preview → R2 sync gated on build success per b0420a0 — gate exercised, 12 files synced)'
first successful deploy whose head (63fd1d0) contains the schema bump 793a093, created 2026-06-30T18:24:09Z; log expired
first successful deploy whose head (b0420a0) contains the fix, created 2026-06-30T18:49:07Z; log expired

notes: exposure: ungated sync installed since the 4/12 chain (715c932) until the gated line was installed from the b0420a0 tree, which the 7/01 audit shows exercised at the 7/01 03:00 ET run; the schema-mismatch consequence needed the 6/30 schema bump (candidate deploy 18:24Z), so no 3am run fell in the harmful window (6/30 3am ran before the bump)

old-schema era (4/12–6/30): whether any 3am chain synced after a failed pull/build is unknown — Route R (cron.log 3am lines); such a sync would have re-uploaded the prior consistent parquets + manifest

deployed basis operator_report: deploys never touch crontab, so the pack's log bound (83a5cad by 7/02) only dates the script on the box; the 7/01 audit dates the installed, exercised gate (live_by = the 7/01 03:00 ET run it describes; not_live_before = the b0420a0 deploy run creation)
kept (not dropped) because R2 is a restore dependency: a manifest/physical-schema mismatch would corrupt restores silently
